description: S47 T7 (MC2, rule 3): tool_show on a name the caller does NOT hold. This is the answer an agent gets for a tool somebody else was granted, for a peer's private MCP tool, and for a name that never existed — ONE sentence, produced by ONE code path, with the nearest names drawn from the caller's OWN held set (`read` and `write` here, because those are what this agent holds). That identity is the whole rule: if an unheld name answered differently from a nonexistent one, this door would answer "does that tool exist?" for anyone who could spell, which is the oracle S46 closed for the MCP own-view reads and which a withheld grant must not hand back. The daemon's TestToolShowOfUnheldEqualsNonexistentSentence pins the byte-identity; this fixture pins the sentence a client sees.

data.what: the own-view read named "acme.post", which is not a tool in your set; the nearest names are: "read", "write"
data.means: the read answered cleanly and the name is simply absent — nothing was written, and this is not the catalog declining to answer (it answers everything it has)
